story.what_it_does: Hindustan Unilever sells everyday household and personal products across Home Care, Beauty & Wellbeing, Personal Care and Foods. In FY2025-26 it had turnover of about ₹61,315 crore from continuing operations, after demerging its ice-cream business into Kwality Wall's on 1 December 2025.
story.plans: Management says growth, especially volume growth, is the priority, and expects FY27 to be better than FY26. It aims to keep EBITDA margin in a guided range, which the latest deck puts at 22-24%, and targets 10% savings from advertising productivity.
story.moat: The notes do not describe the moat directly. The scale of the business (₹18,071 crore quarterly turnover) and its ability to take price rises of 2-5% while volumes still grew suggest some pricing strength, though soaps and Personal Care volumes have been weak.

scenarios.story: Growth keeps accelerating, with sales up 15% and volumes up 7% in the Sep-26 quarter, and Home Care leading. Pricing and productivity savings hold EBITDA margin inside the 22-24% range while volumes keep growing.
signals_to_watch: Underlying volume growth staying at or above the 7% reached in the Sep-26 quarter
EBITDA margin staying within the 22-24% guided range

scenarios.story: Sales growth stays strong, helped by price increases, while profit grows only about 9% before one-offs as margins slip. FY27 ends better than FY26, as guided, with margins near the lower part of the range.
signals_to_watch: Profit after tax before exceptional items growth of around 9%
Price growth relative to volume growth, given 8% price growth in the Sep-26 quarter

scenarios.story: Elevated commodity costs, palm oil and crude-linked inputs, outrun price increases, and growth leans on price rather than volume. Gross margin has already fallen 400 bps and EBITDA margin 140 bps year on year, and a weak monsoon or geopolitical shock could push margins below range.
signals_to_watch: Gross margin and EBITDA margin trend versus the 22% low end of the guided range
Personal Care and soaps volumes, which were flat or declining
